strengths: The paper addresses an important practical problem: improving fine-grained semantic compliance and geometric coherence in text-to-3D generation.
Using VLM Yes/No log-odds as a differentiable reward is intuitive, and applying a common critic to both SDS optimization and native-3D sampling is a potentially useful, moderately original direction.

The optimization-based evaluation covers 110 GPTEval3D prompts and includes numerous established baselines. The qualitative examples suggest improvements in object interactions, attributes, and some spatial relationships.
The manuscript is generally well organized and visually clear, reports approximate runtime and hardware, and honestly acknowledges difficulty with long, detailed prompts.
weaknesses: The central feed-forward guidance mechanism is not specified sufficiently to establish soundness. Equation 10 is explicitly only conceptual: the paper does not explain how a noisy Hunyuan3D latent is decoded, rendered, and differentiated at every denoising step. In particular, mesh extraction commonly includes non-differentiable operations. The claimed 60-second runtime for 50 render-and-Qwen-7B backward passes is also difficult to assess without an algorithm, profiling, or memory details.

The VLM formulation is technically imprecise. Qwen2.5-VL is described as having a binary-classification head, although the relevant quantities would normally be vocabulary-token logits; tokenization and scoring of Yes/No variants are unspecified. The assertion that the entire image-preprocessing, VLM, 3D decoding, and rendering path is differentiable is not demonstrated.

The advertised dual-query critic is actually one conjunctive query requiring both criteria simultaneously. A single Yes/No log-odds value cannot reveal whether content or geometry caused rejection or provide independently controllable objectives. The paper provides no analysis of conflicting gradients, reward saturation, or calibration, and no quantitative ablation separating content and geometry signals.

The feed-forward quantitative evaluation is not credible as reported. Table 2 is evaluated only on the cases shown in Figures 1 and 4, apparently four prompts. FID and CLIP-FID are not meaningful on such a tiny set, while the reference distribution, rendering protocol, and the undefined Geometry score are omitted. There are no error bars, repeated samples, human judgments, or broad prompt benchmark.

The GPTEval3D evidence relies entirely on GPT-4o-mini Elo judgments without human validation, uncertainty estimates, repeated judging, or enough detail about pair construction, view selection, ordering, and aggregation. Thus the numerical margins do not convincingly establish the broad superiority claimed, especially for genuine 3D plausibility.

The qualitative studies and ablations use only selected examples. There is no quantitative ablation of the geometry prompt, multiview input, annealing schedule, VLM backbone, guidance scale, or number of views, and no comparison against simpler semantic-only VLM or CLIP/classifier-guidance alternatives.

Reproducibility is inadequate. Missing details include the number and poses of views, render resolution, exact lambda schedules and guidance scales, optimization settings, latent decoding/rendering procedure, preprocessing, prompt/token-logit implementation, random seeds, evaluator prompts, and metric definitions. The manuscript refers to supplementary implementation details, but no supplement is included.

Baseline fairness is unclear: the text inconsistently names Hunyuan3D 2.0 and 2.1, does not explain how text prompts are converted into inputs for image-conditioned native-3D systems, and does not report matched seeds, conditioning images, or computational budgets.

Several claims are overstated. Multiview 2D judgments do not by themselves prove robust 3D spatial understanding, and the presented experiments do not establish a general critic across diverse representations or models. Calling iterative native-3D diffusion a feed-forward paradigm is also confusing.

Originality is limited by the close relationship to established reward-based SDS and classifier/test-time diffusion guidance; the main novelty is their application with a VLM to 3D, but the paper does not sufficiently distinguish its derivation from those precedents.

The limitations discussion is too narrow. It mentions long prompts but omits the high computational cost, VLM bias and miscalibration, adversarial or reward-hacking behavior, dependence on visible surface evidence, and failure on occluded/internal geometry. No acute ethical issue is evident, but these deployment and bias concerns deserve treatment.

strengths: Originality/significance: Using gradients of VLM Yes/No log-odds as a common critic for both SDS optimization and native-3D diffusion sampling is an intuitive, potentially useful unification. Applying one form of guidance across these two paradigms is more interesting than an isolated prompt-scoring modification.

Soundness: The optimization-based study covers 110 GPTEval3D prompts and compares against a reasonably broad set of established baselines. The reported improvements are consistent across all six benchmark metrics, rather than being confined to text alignment.

Presentation: The paper is visually polished and easy to follow. Equations 5–10 convey the high-level mechanism clearly, and the qualitative figures illustrate relevant semantic, relational, and geometric failure modes.

Limitations: The authors candidly acknowledge failure on fine details in long prompts, exemplified by the missing lifted leg and outstretched arm in the “Embracing Peace” result, and suggest disentangling semantic and geometric feedback.
weaknesses: Soundness—feed-forward evidence: The central test-time-guidance claim is supported by an extremely weak evaluation. Section 5.2 says Table 2 is computed on “all cases shown in Fig. 1 and 4,” apparently only four prompts. FID and CLIP-FID are not reliable or meaningful distributional estimates on such a tiny, selectively displayed set. The geometry metric is not defined, and there are no sample counts, confidence intervals, repeated seeds, or human judgments. Thus Table 2 does not substantiate the claimed broad improvement.

Soundness—underspecified feasibility: Equation 10 is explicitly described as only “conceptual.” The paper does not explain how an intermediate Hunyuan3D latent is decoded into a renderable representation at every denoising step, whether all decoding and surface-extraction operations are differentiable, how cameras are chosen, or how the gradient is normalized and combined with the sampler. These omissions leave the main native-3D contribution technically unverifiable. The claimed 60-second runtime for 50 rounds of decoding, rendering, Qwen2.5-VL-7B backpropagation, and sampling is also not broken down.

Soundness—critic construction: Despite repeatedly calling the method “dual-query,” the implementation uses one conjunctive Yes/No question containing two criteria. A single log-odds value cannot reveal whether rejection is caused by content or geometry, or control their tradeoff. The only relevant ablation is qualitative and cherry-picked; there is no quantitative comparison of joint versus separate critics, alternative prompts, logit scoring choices, or different VLMs.

Evaluation: The 110-prompt experiment relies entirely on GPT-4o-mini pairwise judgments, with no human evaluation or conventional independent metrics. The manuscript does not specify comparison counts, randomization, view selection, evaluator prompts, generation seeds, or uncertainty for the Elo scores. Because the proposed training signal and evaluator are both VLM-based notions of quality, independent human validation is especially important.

Evaluation and significance: Qualitative comparisons show only selected successes, and several do not isolate the proposed intervention. For feed-forward generation, VLM3D is built on Hunyuan3D, while CLAY is merely an additional unguided baseline; guidance is not demonstrated on multiple feed-forward backbones despite broad generality claims. For optimization, the paper provides no cost-matched comparison showing whether improvements survive the substantial 2.2-hour-per-asset computation.

Reproducibility: Essential values and procedures are absent: number and resolution of rendered views, camera distribution, exact lambda schedules and magnitudes, optimizer settings, gradient handling, renderer and 3D representation, token/logit extraction details, metric implementations, and feed-forward benchmark construction. No code, pseudocode, or release commitment is provided. Referring generally to supplementary material does not make the submitted manuscript independently reproducible. Presentation/originality: The paper overstates conclusions with language such as “proves,” “significant,” and “generalizable” without statistical testing or sufficiently broad experiments. Related work also does not adequately position the contribution against prior differentiable VLM/VQA reward and guidance methods, making the degree of methodological novelty difficult to assess.

Limitations and ethics: The limitations section discusses only prompt-detail failures. It omits dependence on VLM calibration and prompt wording, adversarial reward exploitation, demographic and cultural biases, compute/memory overhead, failure to infer true 3D consistency from sparse 2D views, and possible unsafe or copyrighted asset generation. These omissions are not necessarily fatal ethical violations, but they make the treatment of limitations and responsible use inadequate.

strengths: The paper targets important, well-motivated failures in text-to-3D generation: fine-grained semantic alignment and multi-view geometric coherence.
Using a VLM's Yes/No log-odds as a differentiable critic is intuitive, and demonstrating the idea in both SDS optimization and native-3D sampling is potentially original and broadly useful.
The optimization-based evaluation covers 110 GPTEval3D prompts and numerous established baselines; Table 1 reports consistent improvements across all six benchmark metrics.

The qualitative examples are generally compelling, especially for object interactions, prompt perturbations, and obvious part-assembly failures. The geometry-query and multi-view ablations provide useful preliminary evidence for both design choices.
The manuscript is visually clear and includes an honest limitation concerning long, detailed prompts; no material research-ethics concern is apparent.
weaknesses: Soundness is the decisive concern: the feed-forward integration is described only by a conceptual update equation. The paper does not explain how gradients pass from Qwen through rendering and Hunyuan3D's latent decoder/mesh extraction, which generally includes non-differentiable operations. Without the actual differentiable surrogate or implementation, a central technical claim cannot be verified.

The feed-forward quantitative evidence is inadequate. Table 2 is evaluated only on the cases shown in Figures 1 and 4, apparently four prompts, yet reports FID and CLIP-FID, which are not meaningful or stable at that sample size. The 'comprehensive Geometry score' is neither defined nor cited, and no uncertainty or statistical testing is provided.

The feed-forward task and comparison protocol are ambiguous. Hunyuan3D and CLAY are image-conditioned in the presented examples, which include reference images, while the manuscript frames the task as text-to-3D and does not state exactly what conditioning each method receives, how seeds are controlled, or whether paired generations are compared.

The optimization evaluation relies entirely on GPT-4o-mini Elo judgments without human validation, judge-agreement analysis, confidence intervals, or checks for bias from optimizing one VLM and evaluating with another related multimodal model. Consequently, the strong claims of superiority and significance are not yet convincingly supported.

Reproducibility is poor despite the simple high-level description: numerical schedules for lambda_VLM and lambda_TTG, number and selection of views, camera distributions, rendering details, gradient normalization, optimizer settings, prompt formatting/token handling, and sampling modifications are missing. The text claims these details are in supplementary material, but none is included in the submitted manuscript.

The combined conjunctive query does not establish that the critic separately understands semantics and 3D geometry. It yields one scalar, so failures cannot be attributed to either component and competing objectives cannot be balanced. Ablations are qualitative and use different diffusion backbones across rows, further limiting causal conclusions.

The paper does not study robustness to VLM prompt wording, gradient saturation or adversarial exploitation, different VLM backbones, computational overhead relative to baselines, or unsuccessful generations. Generality is therefore overstated based on one VLM, one SDS backbone, and one guided native-3D pipeline.

Presentation is polished at a high level but technically imprecise: Qwen is described as having a binary-classification head although the method appears to use autoregressive token logits, and several implementation-critical assertions are labeled 'conceptual.' These issues prevent others from reliably building on the contribution in its current form.

strengths: The central idea is intuitive and potentially useful: derive a differentiable critic from Qwen2.5-VL Yes/No log-odds over multi-view renderings, then combine it with SDS or use it as test-time guidance for a native 3D diffusion model.

The paper demonstrates breadth by integrating the critic into two substantially different generation pipelines. The reported GPTEval3D Elo improvements over MVDream and preference-based baselines are sizable, and several qualitative examples show better prompt compliance and fewer disconnected parts.

The manuscript is generally understandable and includes pseudocode, optimization ranges, runtime and memory costs, prompt templates, a VLM-only experiment, and ablations of multi-view input and the geometry query.
The limitations section honestly identifies failures on long, detailed prompts and proposes separating semantic and geometric feedback; this is useful and should not be penalized.
weaknesses: Soundness: the feed-forward evaluation is not adequately defined. The Geometry score averages Chamfer, Hausdorff, and point-to-mesh distances, but the manuscript never identifies the reference mesh against which generated meshes are compared. FID and CLIP-FID are reported on only 24 prompts without specifying the reference distribution, number of samples, rendering protocol, or uncertainty. Consequently, Table 2 cannot substantiate the central claim of improved geometric quality.

Soundness: the optimization-based evidence relies entirely on GPT-4o-mini pairwise judgments. There is no human study, confidence interval, repeated-seed analysis, or evaluator-bias check, despite the method optimizing a related VLM signal. Some baseline results are reproduced, while DreamDPO and other results are sourced from papers or repositories, leaving comparability of prompts, renderings, and evaluation runs unclear.

The ablations provide weak causal evidence. Prompt variants are compared using their own VLM rewards, although logits produced under different questions are not calibrated or directly comparable. The geometry-query and multi-view ablations are largely qualitative and use only selected examples; there is no factorial quantitative study separating semantic and geometric effects.

Important method details are underspecified or inconsistent. Qwen2.5-VL is described as having a binary-classification head, although it is an autoregressive model; the exact tokenization and extraction of Yes/No logits are omitted. The number and distribution of camera views, normalization of gradients, exact SDS guidance schedule, and the criterion used to choose prompt-dependent weights in [300,800] are also missing. Equation 10 and Algorithm 2 give different conceptual updates, without deriving the scheduler-dependent scaling needed to modify a diffusion prediction.

Significance and originality are moderate rather than exceptional: using pretrained model logits as differentiable rewards and classifier-style test-time diffusion guidance are established ideas. The cross-paradigm 3D application is interesting, but the evidence does not yet establish the claimed generality because only one principal VLM, one SDS backbone, and one guided native-3D backbone are quantitatively evaluated.

Reproducibility is inadequate. The abstract contains a blank code link, and the supplied manuscript does not include the claimed code package. Prompt lists, seeds, evaluator prompts/settings, reference data for FID and mesh distances, camera configurations, and full baseline protocols are absent. The impact statement is also boilerplate and does not discuss foreseeable misuse, dataset/model biases, or intellectual-property concerns associated with generated 3D assets.

strengths: The central idea is intuitive and potentially useful: backpropagating a VLM’s Yes/No token-logit difference through multi-view renderings provides a simple semantic and geometric guidance signal. Applying the same idea to both SDS optimization and native-3D diffusion sampling is appealing.

The manuscript is generally easy to follow and includes pseudocode, computational costs, qualitative examples, and some useful implementation details. The limitations section honestly acknowledges failures on detailed prompts.

The reported GPTEval3D results on 110 prompts and the qualitative examples suggest that VLM guidance may improve prompt alignment and mitigate visible artifacts. The differentiable image-preprocessing implementation could also be practically useful. weaknesses: Soundness: the feed-forward evaluation is not sufficiently defined to support the central geometric claims. Table 2 uses only 24 prompts; FID is unreliable at this scale, and the paper does not specify the reference distribution. More seriously, its Geometry Score averages Chamfer, Hausdorff, and point-to-mesh distances without identifying the reference meshes against which generated meshes are compared. Consequently, the reported geometric improvement cannot be interpreted or reproduced.

Soundness: Table 1 relies entirely on GPT-4o-mini pairwise judgments, with no human evaluation, evaluator validation, confidence intervals, repeated generations, or significance tests. The paper also mixes newly generated outputs, results sourced from GPTEval3D/threestudio, and DreamDPO numbers copied from its paper. Backbone differences are substantial—for example, the supplement states that DreamReward uses Stable Diffusion 2.1 whereas VLM3D uses MVDream—so the table does not cleanly isolate the proposed critic.

Soundness: several ablations are not probative. Table 4 compares raw rewards produced by different prompts, although these logit scales are not calibrated or comparable; gradient norms likewise do not measure output quality. Table 5 reports only the same critic’s reward, creating a circular selection criterion. Tables 4–7 omit sample counts, variability, and statistical tests, while the prompt-perturbation study contains only two hand-picked examples.

The method is described as a “dual-query” critic, but the implementation is a single conjunctive Yes/No question. This entangles semantic fidelity and geometry, offers no diagnosis when one criterion fails, and does not establish that the model possesses genuine 3D spatial understanding rather than rewarding favorable visible renderings. Occluded or internal geometry cannot be assessed from the presented views.

The feed-forward experiment has important ambiguities. Hunyuan3D is described as image-conditioned through an MVDream-generated reference, while Algorithm 2 instead conditions the denoiser directly on text. The manuscript does not clearly state whether baseline and guided runs receive identical reference images, random seeds, and latent initializations, leaving open whether improvements arise from guidance or changed inputs/sampling.

Reproducibility is inadequate despite the pseudocode. The optimization setting omits the exact number and distribution of camera views, a fully specified annealing schedule, prompt-by-prompt weight choices, seeds, evaluator prompts and pair construction, and mesh-processing details. The suggested initial VLM weight ranges from 300 to 800 based on a subjective assessment of prompt difficulty. The paper also says “Code is available at” without supplying a URL.

Originality is moderate rather than strong. Differentiating selected language-model logits through a frozen multimodal model is a straightforward extension of existing differentiable reward and test-time guidance ideas. The differentiable preprocessor and application to two 3D pipelines are useful engineering, but the manuscript overstates this as a principled general framework without comparisons against alternative VLM critics, continuous scoring formulations, or other guidance objectives.

Presentation contains overclaims such as “proves,” “spatial intelligence,” and “outperforms all baselines” that are not justified by the limited and confounded evidence. The visual results are attractive but appear selectively chosen and are not backed by a blinded human preference study or multi-seed analysis.

The limitations discussion is welcome but too narrow: it focuses mainly on long prompts and omits evaluator bias, adversarial/reward-hacking behavior, view-selection dependence, computational cost, and dependence on one VLM. The ethics statement is boilerplate and dismisses foreseeable issues such as inherited VLM biases, copyrighted 3D content, misuse, and the considerable 49–53 GB memory footprint. Overall, the idea is promising, but unresolved evaluation and reproducibility defects prevent reliable confidence in the main claims.

strengths: The paper presents a promising and practically useful idea: extracting a differentiable Yes/No log-odds signal from a VLM and backpropagating it through multi-view rendering. Applying the same critic to both SDS optimization and native-3D diffusion guidance is an interesting contribution.

The qualitative results are compelling. Examples involving interacting figures, subtle spatial relations, and malformed Hunyuan3D outputs indicate improvements in prompt fidelity and part assembly that are difficult to obtain from CLIP-style objectives alone.

The optimization-based evaluation is reasonably broad: 110 GPTEval3D prompts, several established baselines, and improvements across all six reported criteria. The appendix also adds useful runtime, memory, scheduling, prompt, and VLM-only ablations.

The method and motivation are presented clearly. The distinction between iterative SDS optimization and test-time guidance during native-3D sampling is explained well, and the pseudocode makes both integrations understandable.

The limitations section honestly identifies difficulty with long, detailed prompts and proposes sensible future work on disentangling semantic and geometric feedback. The societal risk of this particular technical contribution appears limited.
weaknesses: The feed-forward evaluation is too underspecified to support its central claims. Table 2 uses only 24 prompts; the reference distribution for FID and CLIP-FID is not defined, and FID is unreliable at this sample size. The reported Geometry score requires reference meshes for Chamfer, Hausdorff, and point-to-mesh distances, but the manuscript never explains where such ground-truth meshes come from or how the three differently scaled distances are normalized before averaging.

The main evidence relies heavily on automated evaluators: GPT-4o-mini Elo for GPTEval3D, CLIP-derived metrics, and the proposed geometric metric. There is no human study despite claims of “human-preferred” assets, no confidence intervals or repeated-seed analysis, and no statistical testing. This is particularly concerning because the gains could depend strongly on random initialization and prompt selection.

The ablations do not adequately isolate the claimed mechanisms. Table 4 compares each prompt using that prompt's own VLM reward, making reward magnitudes across formulations difficult to interpret; Table 5 likewise selects schedules using the optimized reward rather than independent quality measures. The geometry-query and multi-view ablations are principally qualitative, and Figure 7 changes the diffusion backbone between rows.

What is called a “dual-query” is actually one conjunctive Yes/No query containing two criteria. It provides no separate semantic and geometric signals, so the paper cannot establish which criterion drives a gradient or whether trade-offs between them are handled reliably. A VLM observing rendered views can also detect visible multi-view artifacts, but this alone does not justify the broader claim of robust 3D spatial understanding.

The claimed generality is overstated. Each paradigm is demonstrated with essentially one primary pipeline: MVDream for SDS and Hunyuan3D for native-3D guidance. Moreover, the feed-forward implementation first generates an image with MVDream and then runs an image-to-3D model, while the main presentation and Algorithm 2 suggest direct text conditioning. Baseline input conditions are not clearly matched, especially for the online CLAY system.

Important reproducibility details remain missing or ambiguous, including the number and distribution of rendered views, optimizer and renderer settings, exact optimization-side guidance schedule, tokenization/logit extraction for Qwen's generative output, random seeds, mesh normalization and metric implementation, and the exact composition of the 24-prompt test set. The stated 49–53 GB memory requirements also limit accessibility.

The impact statement is perfunctory and overlooks foreseeable misuse involving deceptive synthetic assets, copyrighted designs, and dataset/model biases. These are not decisive ethical barriers, but they deserve acknowledgment. Overall, the idea and qualitative results are promising, yet the evaluation gaps prevent the central semantic-and-geometric improvement claims from being considered sufficiently established for acceptance.
